html:
The Republic of Turkey was proclaimed on 29 October 1923 by the Grand National Assembly in Ankara, with Mustafa Kemal as its first president. It replaced the Ottoman Empire in Anatolia and eastern Thrace.

After defeat in the First World War, the Allies had planned in the Treaty of Sèvres to divide Anatolia among Greece, Armenia, France, Italy and Kurdish self-rule. A nationalist government in Ankara fought the War of Independence and drove out the Greek army in 1922. The Assembly ended the sultanate that year. The Treaty of Lausanne, signed in July 1923, recognised the new state's borders, and Ankara became the capital.

Lausanne also agreed the population exchange of Orthodox Christians and Muslims between Greece and Turkey. The new republic soon abolished the caliphate and began the secular reforms that defined it.
sum: The Republic of Turkey was proclaimed on 29 October 1923 by the Grand National Assembly in Ankara, with Mustafa Kemal as its first president. It replaced the Ottoman Empire in Anatolia and eastern Thrace.
